chosenStory: Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger owner to cut 4% of workforce
whyThisStory: The workforce cuts offer a sharper luxury-insider joke than the growth, ownership and data stories: an expensive fashion-house seat made less functional by a very small saving.
sceneDescription: An exquisite executive chair has had a small section sawn off one leg to save material, leaving the expensive seat precariously supported—a literal-minded response to PVH cutting staff to reduce costs. In a fashion-house director’s pale, quietly luxurious office, a carved walnut chair with gilt details and ivory silk upholstery stands beside a travertine desk. One front leg ends noticeably above the floor; its matching offcut lies directly beneath it. An unmarked brass-backed handsaw rests across the seat. Everything else is perfectly respectable.
finalImagePrompt: A fashion-house director’s private office, pale plaster wall above a travertine desk edge and lightly scuffed oak floor. Middle of frame, lower half, a small carved walnut chair with gilt details and ivory silk upholstery occupies roughly one third of the width. One front leg has its bottom section neatly sawn off; the matching offcut lies beneath the gap. An unmarked brass-backed handsaw rests on the seat. Soft window daylight, real shadows, visible sawdust and worn gilding. Plain upper wall.
